subtitle: From Anandpur’s Call to the Eternal Guru

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Guru Gobind Singh and the Panj Pyare against a glowing sky
panels.action: Guru Gobind Singh stands tall in gleaming turban and arms, flanked by the five beloved ones in distinct turbans and dress, as a vast gathering of Sikhs stretches into the haze of Anandpur’s hills behind them.

dialogue.text: On Vaisakhi at Anandpur, 1699, Guru Gobind Singh called for five lives—and forged the Khalsa, a fearless sangat whose story would end with scripture, not a sword, as the eternal Guru.

i18n.hi: वैसाखी १६९९, आनंदपुर। गुरु गोबिंद सिंह ने पाँच जिंदगियाँ माँगीं – और गढ़ी खालसा, निडर संगत, जिसकी कहानी तलवार नहीं, गुरुग्रंथ पर खत्म हुई।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Anandpur Sahib from a high hillside at sunrise
panels.action: From a misty hillside, Anandpur Sahib appears below: white fort-walls, clustered houses, and tents filled with pilgrims as orange flags flutter in the cool light of dawn.

dialogue.text: By 1699, Anandpur Sahib had become more than a town. It was a refuge for the hunted, a training ground for the faithful, and the seat of a Guru shaped by martyrdom and war.

i18n.hi: १६९९ तक आनंदपुर साहिब महज़ नगर नहीं रहा। यह मज़लूमों की पनाह, विश्वासियों की रणभूमि, और शहीदी व जंग से ढले गुरु की गद्दी बन चुका था।

panels.shot: medium shot of young Guru Gobind Singh in Patna, with a ghosted overlay of his father in chains
panels.action: A youthful Gobind Rai in Patna gazes out a balcony, toy bow in hand, while the faint, solemn image of Guru Tegh Bahadur in chains before an imperial court looms behind him like a memory.

dialogue.text: Gobind Rai, born in Patna in 1666, became Guru after his father Tegh Bahadur chose death rather than forced conversion. That choice burned into the son a new resolve.

i18n.hi: गोबिंद राय, जिनका जन्म १६६६ में पटना में हुआ, पिता तेग बहादुर की शहादत के बाद गुरु बने – जब पिता ने ज़ुल्म के आगे धर्म बदलने से मौत चुन ली। वही आग बेटे के दिल में धधक उठी।

panels.shot: dynamic oblique wide of Anandpur’s training ground
panels.action: On a dusty field near Anandpur, Guru Gobind Singh rides a horse, shouting instructions as men and boys practice archery and swordplay, some in farmer’s clothes, some in soldier’s mail.

dialogue.text: In Anandpur he trained peasants and artisans to ride, shoot and stand as warriors. His hukamnamas already spoke of a Khalsa—his community of the committed—before 1699 formalized it in form and discipline.

i18n.hi: आनंदपुर में उन्होंने किसानों और कारीगरों को घुड़सवारी, बंदूक, तलवार – सब सिखाया। उनके हुक्मनामों में ‘खालसा’ – यानी समर्पित समुदाय – १६९९ से पहले ही झलकने लगा था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of the Vaisakhi gathering at Anandpur
panels.action: A packed field outside Anandpur sways with turbans and shawls as men and women gather under bright canopies, their faces turned toward a raised platform where Guru Gobind Singh stands beneath a fluttering banner.

dialogue.text: On Vaisakhi, April 1699, they came by the thousands. Farmers from the Doab, artisans from Lahore, traders from Delhi, even distant villagers—drawn by news that the Guru would reveal a new path.

i18n.hi: वैसाखी, अप्रैल १६९९ पर हज़ारों उमड़े। दोआब के किसान, लाहौर के कारीगर, दिल्ली के व्यापारी, दूर-दराज़ गाँवों के लोग – सुनकर कि गुरु कोई नया मार्ग दिखाएँगे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Guru Gobind Singh addressing the sangat
panels.action: Guru Gobind Singh stands on the platform in saffron robes and blue turban, sword at his side, right arm outstretched toward the gathered Sikhs, eyes intense, as a charged hush falls over the crowd.

dialogue.text: He spoke of tyranny and fear, of the need to stand as protectors. Then, to a stunned sangat, he asked, in some accounts, for a head—for those willing to give everything, even life.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने ज़ुल्म और डर की बात की, और रखवाला बन खड़े होने की। फिर, हैरान संगत के बीच, कुछ रिवायतों में, उन्होंने माँगा – एक सिर – जो सब कुछ, जान तक देने को तैयार हो।

panels.shot: slow push-in on one hesitant crowd, with one man stepping forward
panels.action: In the sea of anxious faces, a middle-aged man from Lahore, Bhai Daya Ram, steps forward with steady eyes while those beside him shrink back and trade uneasy glances.

dialogue.text: Sikh tradition remembers five who answered: Daya Ram the shopkeeper from Lahore, Dharam Das from Hastinapur, Himmat from Jagannath’s coast, Mohkam from Gujarat, Sahib Chand from the forests of Nangal.

i18n.hi: सिख रिवायत पाँच नाम याद रखती है: लाहौर का दुकानदार दया राम, हस्तिनापुर का धरम दास, जगन्नाथ तट का हिम्मत, गुजरात का मोखम, नंगल के जंगलों का साहिब चंद।

panels.shot: composed medium-wide of the five volunteers standing before the Guru
panels.action: On the platform, the five men kneel in a row before Guru Gobind Singh, each in clothing that hints at a different region and craft, as the Guru looks upon them with fierce, proud tenderness.

dialogue.speaker: guru_gobind_singh_and_the_panj_pyare
dialogue.text: From many lands, one house. From many castes, one Khalsa.

i18n.hi: कितने देस, एक देहरा। कितनी जातें, एक खालसा।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of the preparation of Amrit
panels.action: Guru Gobind Singh kneels over an iron bowl filled with clean water and sugar crystals, stirring with a double-edged sword as the five kneel around him, hands folded, eyes lowered in devotion.

dialogue.text: He mixed water and sweetness in an iron bowl and stirred with a sword, reciting divine hymns. The sweetened steel would bind them to courage and compassion at once.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने लोहे के बर्तन में पानी और मिठास मिलाई, तलवार से घोला, और गुरुबाणी का पाठ किया। यह मीठी तेज़ी उन्हें एक साथ साहस और दया से बाँधने वाली थी।

panels.shot: tight medium of Amrit being given to one of the five
panels.action: Guru Gobind Singh gently raises the bowl to Bhai Daya Ram’s lips as the others watch; behind them, a few women and men strain for a glimpse, faces filled with awe and uncertainty.

dialogue.text: He administered the Amrit to each, making them the Panj Pyare—the Five Beloved. They took new names ending in Singh, lion, shedding caste labels that had chained their world.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने हर एक को अमृत पिलाया, और उन्हें बनाया ‘पंज प्यारे’ – पाँच प्यारे। सबको नया नाम मिला, ‘सिंह’ – शेर – और जाति के लगाम छोड़ फेंके गए।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Guru Gobind Singh kneeling before the Panj Pyare
panels.action: In a startling reversal, Guru Gobind Singh kneels before the five, hands joined, as they stand above him holding the iron bowl, their faces a mix of humility and astonished responsibility.

dialogue.text: Then he did what few leaders dared: he asked the five to initiate him. In their hands, not above them, he placed his own identity, showing that Khalsa authority flowed through the sangat.

i18n.hi: फिर उन्होंने वह किया जो कम ही नेता कर पाते हैं – पाँचों से कहा, अब तुम मुझे दीक्षा दो। अपनी ही पहचान उन्होंने उनके हाथों सौंप दी, दिखाया कि खालसा की ताकत संगत से बहती है।

panels.shot: side-on wide of Khalsa initiation of men and women
panels.action: The Panj Pyare stand by the iron bowl as lines of men and women step forward—farmers, artisans, soldiers—some cutting off old braids, some adjusting turbans, all receiving the Amrit one by one.

dialogue.text: Soon many more came. Men and women received the same Amrit, the same code. A visible discipline grew—the uncut hair, the steel bangle, the comb, the sword, the sewn undergarment—marks of a shared, watchful life.

i18n.hi: जल्दी ही और भी उमड़े। औरतें-पुरुष, एक ही अमृत, एक ही मर्यादा। एक दिखने वाला अनुशासन उभरा – केश, कड़ा, कंघा, किरपान, कच्छा – जागते समुदाय की नज़र आने वाली निसानियाँ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Gobind Singh addressing newly initiated Khalsa
panels.action: Guru Gobind Singh stands before rows of freshly initiated Khalsa, their turbans firm, kirpans at their sides, as he raises his hand in oath, the Panj Pyare standing slightly behind him.

dialogue.speaker: guru_gobind_singh_and_the_panj_pyare
dialogue.text: You are my Khalsa. Recognize no one as master but the One, fear none, protect all.

i18n.hi: तुम मेरा खालसा हो। एक अकाल से सिवा किसी को मालिक मत मानो, किसी से डरो मत, सबकी रखवाली करो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Anandpur under siege with Khalsa on the ramparts
panels.action: Walls of Anandpur bristle with Khalsa defenders as Mughal and hill-state forces camp below; flags flutter in the wind while smoke from campfires rises into a brooding sky.

dialogue.text: The new Khalsa did not remain an idea. Mughal power and allied hill chiefs besieged Anandpur. Hunger, rain and treachery pressed against the walls as oaths of loyalty were tested.

i18n.hi: खालसा बस खयाल नहीं रहा। मुग़ल ताकत और पहाड़ी राजे मिलकर आनंदपुर घेर बैठे। भूख, बरसात, और विश्वासघात क़िले की दीवारों पर बरसे, जब वफ़ादारी की कसमें आज़माई गईं।

panels.shot: night-time medium of Guru Gobind Singh consulting with a small group including the Panj Pyare
panels.action: By lamplight in a simple tent, Guru Gobind Singh leans over a rough map with the Panj Pyare and other Sikhs, their faces tired yet resolute, shadows deepening around them.

dialogue.text: Sources differ on each detail, but not on the pattern. Again and again, decisions were taken in counsel—with trusted Sikhs like the Panj Pyare—balancing survival against the duty to keep faith.

i18n.hi: विवरणों में मतभेद होंगे, पर ढाँचा वही है – बार-बार फैसले मशवरे में हुए। भरोसेमंद सिखों, खासकर पंज प्यारे, के साथ – ज़िंदा रहने की राह और ईमान बचाए रखने का फ़र्ज़ तौला गया।

panels.shot: charged wide shot of the fort of Chamkaur at dawn
panels.action: The small fort of Chamkaur stands against a grey dawn as ranks of Mughal troops mass outside; within the walls, a thin line of Khalsa prepare, their silhouettes stark against the courtyard.

dialogue.text: In December 1704 or 1705, at Chamkaur, a handful of Khalsa held a fort against a flood of imperial troops. There, the Khalsa ideal was tested in battle and in the painful choice to preserve the Guru.

i18n.hi: दिसंबर १७०४ या १७०५, चमकौर। मुट्ठी भर खालसा, किले में, बादशाह की लहराती फ़ौज के सामने। यहीं खालसा की कसौटी जंग में भी लगी, और उस कठिन निर्णय में भी कि गुरु को बचाना ही होगा।

panels.shot: intense medium of the Panj Pyare urging Guru Gobind Singh inside the fort
panels.action: Inside Chamkaur’s walls, Guru Gobind Singh stands with bow and sword, ready to continue the fight, as the Panj Pyare face him solemnly, one lifting a hand in earnest appeal.

dialogue.speaker: guru_gobind_singh_and_the_panj_pyare
dialogue.text: Guru ji, the Khalsa commands: you must live, for the Panth.

i18n.hi: गुरु जी, खालसा का हुक्म है – ਆਪ ਜੀ को पंथ के लिए जीना होगा।

panels.shot: close-up on Guru Gobind Singh’s conflicted face as he listens
panels.action: A close view shows Guru Gobind Singh’s face lit by firelight, eyes reddened with fatigue and loss yet softening with acceptance as he listens to the solemn words of his beloved Sikhs.

dialogue.text: Tradition holds that at Chamkaur the Panj Pyare invoked the authority he had given them and ordered the Guru to escape. In obeying, he showed that no one, not even the Guru, stood above the Khalsa’s collective will.

i18n.hi: रिवायत कहती है, चमकौर में पंज प्यारे ने वही अधिकार जगाया जो गुरु ने उन्हें दिया था – और गुरु को निकल जाने का आदेश दिया। गुरु ने मानकर दिखा दिया कि खालसा की सामूहिक रज़ा से ऊपर कोई नहीं – गुरु भी नहीं।

panels.shot: somber wide of the Sarovar at Sirhind with a faint overlay of children
panels.action: A still pool near Sirhind reflects a cloudy sky, while faint, translucent figures of two young boys in regal robes stand at its edge, their eyes calm, as a grim fortress looms in the distance.

dialogue.text: Soon after, his younger sons were bricked alive at Sirhind according to Sikh tradition. Whatever the precise details, the loss deepened the Guru’s break with Mughal authority and his resolve to anchor the Panth beyond his own body.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही समय बाद, सिख परंपरा के अनुसार, उनके छोटे साहिबज़ादों को सिरहिंद में ज़िंदा दीवारों में चुनवा दिया गया। बात जैसे भी रही हो, इस सदमे ने गुरु का मुग़ल हुकूमत से रिश्ता तोड़ डाला और पंथ को अपने ही बल पर टिकाने का इरादा और पक्का हुआ।

panels.shot: wide of Nanded on the Godavari river at sunset
panels.action: At Nanded, the Godavari glows in the sunset as palm trees sway; on the bank, a modest camp of tents and horses rests, with a white canopy sheltering the Guru’s seat.

dialogue.text: Years later, in 1708, far from Punjab on the banks of the Godavari at Nanded, his path neared its end. Yet his final act would lift the Khalsa beyond the life of any single leader.

i18n.hi: सालों बाद, १७०८ में, पंजाब से दूर, नांदेड़ में गोदावरी के किनारे, उनका सफर आख़िरी मोड़ पर था। पर उनका अंतिम क़दम खालसा को किसी एक शरीर से कहीं आगे उठा ले गया।

panels.shot: reverent medium of Guru Gobind Singh before the Guru Granth Sahib
panels.action: Inside a simple tent, Guru Gobind Singh sits cross-legged before the Guru Granth Sahib resting on a low platform, its silk rumala lifted back, while a few Sikhs, including one of the Panj Pyare, kneel around him.

dialogue.speaker: guru_gobind_singh_and_the_panj_pyare
dialogue.text: The Granth is now the Guru. The Khalsa is its living body.

i18n.hi: अब गुरुग्रंथ ही गुरु है। खालसा उसकी जीती-जागती देह है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from the scripture and gathered Sikhs in the tent
panels.action: The view widens to show the Guru Granth Sahib at the center, Guru Gobind Singh slightly behind it, and the Sikhs—men and women, farmers and soldiers—arrayed around in a circle, their heads bowed together.

dialogue.text: With this act, he ended the line of human Gurus. Scripture and community would guide the Panth. The Khalsa, shaped years earlier at Anandpur by the call to courage and equality, was left to walk history as both student and guardian.

i18n.hi: इस एक फ़ैसले से उन्होंने मनुष्य गुरु की परंपरा समेट दी। अब ग्रंथ और गुरुसंगत ही पंथ की राह दिखाएँगे। आनंदपुर की वैसाखी पर साहस और समानता से गढ़ा खालसा, इतिहास में आगे चल पड़ा – शागिर्द भी, निगहबान भी।

panels.shot: timeless low-angle tableau of the Panj Pyare walking forward with modern silhouettes faint behind them
panels.action: The Panj Pyare stride together toward the viewer across an abstract plain, their forms sharp and confident, while faint silhouettes of later generations—farmers, soldiers, migrants, citizens—overlap behind them like echoes in time.

dialogue.text: From Anandpur to Nanded, Guru Gobind Singh showed that courage shared becomes community, and authority shared becomes freedom. The Panj Pyare’s step forward still asks each age: will you stand, not alone, but together?

i18n.hi: आनंदपुर से नांदेड़ तक, गुरु गोबिंद सिंह ने दिखाया – बाँटा हुआ साहस बनता है संगत, बाँटी हुई सत्ता बनती है आज़ादी। तब पंज प्यारे आगे बढ़े थे – आज भी हर दौर से पूछते हैं: क्या तुम अकेले नहीं, साथ खड़े होगे?

title_i18n.en: Guru Gobind Singh Calls the Five
title_i18n.hi: गुरु गोबिंद सिंह की पाँचों को पुकार

subtitle_i18n.en: From Anandpur’s Call to the Eternal Guru
subtitle_i18n.hi: आनंदपुर की पुकार से सनातन गुरु तक
